findings.title: `import()` expressions in object literal are evaluated eagerly on module load
findings.body: In `packages/app-store/index.ts`, each entry is written as `applecalendar: import("./applecalendar")` rather than a factory function `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`. Because the `import(...)` calls are not wrapped in functions, JavaScript evaluates every dynamic `import()` immediately when `@calcom/app-store` is imported, loading all 28 app modules in parallel on startup instead of lazily loading only the app being accessed. To defer loading until an app is actually used, make each property a function returning the `import()` promise (and call it at the access sites).

findings.title: Async `forEach` callback causes `apiDeletes` to be populated after `Promise.all` runs
findings.body: When cancelling all remaining bookings of a recurring event (lines 458-470), `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { ... })` is used. Because `Array.prototype.forEach` does not await async callbacks, execution pauses at `await getCalendar(credential)` (line 461) and `await calendar?.deleteEvent(...)` (line 466), while the outer `handler` function continues immediately to `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` at line 652 before any calendar deletion promises have been pushed into `apiDeletes`. As a result, calendar event deletions for recurring bookings are not awaited before the handler returns (and in serverless environments may be terminated before completing), and `apiDeletes` ends up holding resolved values instead of promises.
